oh_trash_shoot_wall.blurb: A west-facing wall in the Mad River Gorge preserve of southwest Ohio, set apart from the busier walls nearby and a calmer place to climb on a weekend. Nineteen lines in all: sixteen are bolted sport routes, with a lone trad line and a couple of boulder problems. Grades range from easy 5.6 and 5.8 climbs up to the 5.11 range, and the bulk of the sport routes sit between 5.10 and 5.11. Expect a blend of older favourites and newer additions. The bases of many routes are steeply undercut, particularly toward the right, so a stick clip is worth bringing. The wall picks up afternoon sun.
oh_trash_shoot_wall.approach: Follow the main path west past Mike's Wall for roughly 200 feet, then drop down a side trail to the left of the rail-trail into the low wet ground. Pass two boulders on the way, and about 50 feet beyond them climb back up a left-hand trail to the cliff line. Watch for loose rock near the top of that last trail.

oh_roadside_highballs.blurb: A small bouldering area in the Bears Den Cabin zone of Mill Creek Metroparks, near Youngstown in northeast Ohio. Two long sandstone faces stand right beside the road, each around 15 to 20 feet tall, so the problems here are tall and committing rather than low and playful. Seventeen problems are recorded, running from very easy to double-digit hard, with most in the V2 to V5 range. The faces are still being cleaned of moss and dirt, so expect some grime and bring a brush. A few pull-offs along the road put the rock a few steps from the car.

oh_west_wall.blurb: A bouldering-only wall on the west side of Sawyer Quarry Nature Preserve, a former quarry outside Perrysburg in northwest Ohio, about eight miles from Toledo. The stone is cut quarry face, and the seventeen problems are short, mostly in the easy to moderate range from V0 to V4, with the bulk at V1 and V2. Quality varies, though several lines pick up good ratings. This is a gentle spot for beginners and for a quick session with friends. To reach it, take the stairs into the quarry and either follow the top shelf of stone around, or descend and walk the brief path over from the eastern bouldering wall.

oh_sand_hill.blurb: A quiet boulder cluster in Great Seal State Park, a short drive from Chillicothe in southern Ohio. The setting is shaded and secluded, and the sandstone is hit or miss, so it rewards climbers happy to explore. Seventeen problems are established, all bouldering: most fall between V1 and V3, with a few V4s and a single harder test, and there is one very easy warm-up. Few lines are developed so far, and there is room for more. It sits a moderate hike from the trailhead lot, so bring your pads and expect to carry them in.

oh_lower_lunch.blurb: The larger half of the Lunch Boulders at Flat Rocks, inside Keller Kirn Park in Lancaster, central Ohio. Sixteen boulder problems on sandstone, which is delicate and best treated gently. Grades run from V0 up to V7, but most are in the V0 to V4 range, which makes it a friendly place for climbers building up. Several of the lines are well-liked classics at V0 and V3. The area is a short walk from the park, and climbers should watch for flying discs from the disc golf course on the way out. The sandstone also includes a crumbly roof, so check holds before trusting them.

oh_east_wall_2.blurb: A shaded wall of highball slabs in Mill Creek Metroparks in northeast Ohio, beside the road in the Roadside Highballs zone. Sixteen bouldering problems range from V0 to V9, with most between V2 and V5 and a couple of hard ones at the top end. Low on the wall, small crimps follow seams in the rock, while higher up the holds turn to sloppers and jugs for the topout. Footholds are small and sparse. The wall is still being cleaned: moss lingers low and loose dirt sits at the top, so topping out can be hazardous. It is only a few steps from where you park.
